# Design a phased data-center campus on a wetland-divided greenfield parcel as a 3D BIM model (`p6_002`)

## Situation

You are the site engineer for a two-hall data-center campus on a rectangular greenfield parcel. Two delineated wetlands divide the southern and northern developable areas, leaving one narrow upland corridor between them. The campus is delivered in two phases; each phase must stand alone as a working facility with complete power, access, and services. The authority having jurisdiction has issued a Development Standards and Conditions of Approval document. Every binding design requirement appears in that prose.

## Inputs

- `agent_view.json`: site geometry, two-phase building program, objective weights, network output schema, and the full `brief_document`. Coordinates use metres in a local CRS. Treat these instance data as authoritative.
- `docs/ifc_contract.md`: required IFC conventions.
- `docs/example.ifc`: a complete toy-site example demonstrating those conventions.
- `submission/model.ifc`: a valid IFC header and empty site to build upon.
- `oracle_client.py`: present in the workspace but unusable in this blind evaluation (see Verification).

## Goal

Place both data halls, the substation, generator yard, cooling plant, landscape berm, and stormwater retention area. Route the road and medium-voltage networks so that all 17 binding requirements are satisfied. A passing design is FEASIBLE. Among feasible designs, minimize `1.0 × MV-cable length + 0.3 × road length`; feasibility takes priority over optimization.

## Constraints

- The binding setbacks, separations, noise limits, stormwater sizing rules, phase requirements, and design-to-cost caps appear only in the prose brief. Some clauses refer to schedules elsewhere in the document, and some do not bind this site.
- Provide one continuous road network from one approved entrance on the designated frontage. Disconnected frontage stubs are not separate entrances and do not satisfy access.
- Buildings and roads must respect the wetland exclusions and buffers. Linear medium-voltage utilities may cross a wetland; roads and structures may not.
- The noise calculation treats each equipment footprint centroid as a point source at the greater of the building height and 2 m, uses a receiver height of 1.5 m, applies spherical spreading of `Lw − 20 log10(d) − 11 dB`, and energetically sums all sources. An intervening structure or berm that blocks the three-dimensional line of sight provides 10 dB insertion loss.
- Deliver an IFC4 BIM model as raw STEP text. The workspace contains no BIM library. Model each program building as an `IfcBuilding` with an extruded-solid footprint and the required identity property set. Embed the road, medium-voltage, and graph payload in the `DCD_Networks` property set on the `IfcSite`.

## Verification (blind evaluation)
This is a blind evaluation: no oracle is served in this run. `python3 oracle_client.py submission/model.ifc` cannot connect, and the verification protocol described in `Task.md` does not apply. The verifier and its libraries are not available in the workspace, and no score, verdict, or other feedback is returned before you submit. Plan the design and IFC serialization to correctness before submitting.
Scoring of the final `submission/model.ifc`: `1.0` for a FEASIBLE design; otherwise one half of the fraction of the 17 binding requirements satisfied; `0.0` when the model fails an IFC parse, extraction, semantic, schema, or geometry gate.

## Expected output

Submit `submission/model.ifc`. The final grade uses the final file only. Feasible models score `1.0`; infeasible extracted models receive the partial-credit score described above; hard-gate failures score `0.0`.

# DCBim p6_002 (v1.3) — data-center site design as a 3D BIM model

Design the data-center site specified in **`agent_view.json`** — read it
first. It contains the site geometry (`site`), the building program
(`program`), objective weights (`objective`), the `output_schema` for the
networks/graph payload, and `brief_document`: the DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS
AND CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL. Coordinates are meters in a local CRS. The
design problem (constraints, objective) is identical to the 2D site-layout
benchmark; what changes is the deliverable:

Your deliverable is **`submission/model.ifc`** — an IFC4 BIM model (STEP
text) of the site: one IfcBuilding with an extruded-solid footprint per
program building, identity psets, and the roads/MV/graph payload embedded
as the `DCD_Networks` pset on the IfcSite. The FULL contract is
**`docs/ifc_contract.md`**; **`docs/example.ifc`** is a complete worked
example (toy site) demonstrating every convention — study it. A stub
model.ifc (valid header, site, no buildings) is provided.

There are NO BIM libraries in this workspace. Producing valid IFC STEP
text is part of the task.

**Every numeric limit that binds your design lives ONLY in the prose of
`brief_document`** — setbacks, separations, noise limits, sizing rules,
access requirements. Some clauses reference schedules elsewhere in the
document; follow the chain. Some clauses do not bind this particular
site; deciding which is part of the task.

## Verification protocol (metered L1 oracle)

The verifier is NOT in this workspace. Your ONLY feedback channel is:

```
python3 oracle_client.py submission/model.ifc
```

- **Budget: 20 calls for this task.** Each call uploads your model. IFC
  gate failures return the verdict (`IFC_INVALID` /
  `EXTRACTION_FAILED`) plus `item:code` tokens (see the contract table).
  Once your model extracts, calls return the design verdict
  (`FEASIBLE | INFEASIBLE | SCHEMA_INVALID | GEOMETRY_INVALID`), the
  failing layer, and failing constraint ids (composites expand, e.g.
  `c12[c1,c8]`). No margins, no distances.
- Call 21 and later are refused (HTTP 429). There is no other oracle
  access and no local verifier.
- **Your session is graded on the BEST design among all oracle-checked
  models plus your final `submission/model.ifc`** (ordered by layer
  reached, then constraint fraction, then lower objective). Every model
  you send counts; a late bad edit cannot erase an earlier good design.

Budget strategy is part of the task: reason the design AND the IFC
serialization to correctness on paper before spending calls, then repair
surgically from the failure codes.

## Scoring

A task pass requires verdict `FEASIBLE` on your final design (every
binding condition satisfied; IFC gates, schema and geometry are hard
gates). Partial credit is one half of the constraint fraction of your
final extracted design. The weighted objective
(`1.0 * mv_cable_length + 0.3 * road_length`) does not change the
score: feasibility is what is graded.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DCBim v1.0 verifier oracle client.

The verifier for this task runs on a metered oracle server, NOT in this
workspace. You may call it at most 20 times for this task. Each call
uploads your IFC model and returns diagnostic level L1:

  - IFC gate failures: verdict IFC_INVALID or EXTRACTION_FAILED plus
    failing-item tokens only (e.g. "units:not_metre", "DH1:no_body",
    "DH1:multi_polygon", "file:no_buildings", "scale:scale_implausible")
    -- no line numbers, no exception text.
  - Design verdicts (model extracted OK): FEASIBLE | INFEASIBLE |
    SCHEMA_INVALID | GEOMETRY_INVALID with the failing layer and failing
    constraint ids only (composites expand, e.g. "c12[c1,c8]") -- no
    margins, no distances.

Usage:
    python3 oracle_client.py submission/model.ifc

When the budget is exhausted the server answers HTTP 429. Your session is
graded on the BEST design among all oracle-checked models plus your final
submission/model.ifc (ordered by layer reached, then constraint fraction,
then lower objective) -- so every model you check counts.
"""
import base64
import json
import sys
import urllib.request
import urllib.error
from pathlib import Path

ORACLE_URL = "http://172.17.0.1:18200/check"


def main() -> None:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(2)
    ifc_bytes = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes()
    instance_id = json.loads(
        (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "agent_view.json")
        .read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["id"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        ORACLE_URL,
        data=json.dumps({
            "instance": instance_id,
            "ifc_b64": base64.b64encode(ifc_bytes).decode("ascii"),
        }).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
            print(resp.read().decode())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print(e.read().decode())
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---
name: engineering-deliverables
description: Method for engineering design and calculation packages graded against requirements - document precedence, superseded documents, requirement/constraint registers, hard-constraint checks, unit discipline, optimisation within constraints, and schema-exact deliverable files (CSV, JSON, XLSX, ZIP, IFC). Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.
---

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.

# Site civil design (practising engineer's checks)

Project documents, the local design manual and the reviewing agency's criteria govern; "typical" values are defaults
for when the record is silent - say so. Spillways/rational/Manning/HGL: stormwater-drainage-checks; shoring, settlement,
compaction: geotechnical-checks. Order: criteria and datum (NAVD88 vs NGVD29; ft, US survey ft, m) -> existing
conditions -> layout -> grading -> hydrology/drainage -> utilities -> ESC -> quantities -> cross-check sheets vs calcs.

## 1. Grading and accessibility
- Slope % = rise/run x 100; H:V = run:rise. 2:1 = 50 %, 3:1 = 33.3 %, 4:1 = 25 %, 1:12 = 8.33 %, 1:20 = 5 %,
  1:48 = 2.08 %. Spot elevation between points: E = E1 + s d; horizontal distance between contours d = dz/s.
- Typical minimums: asphalt 1.0 % (1.5 % preferred), concrete 0.5 %, gutter flowline 0.5 %, lawn 2 %, grass swale
  1-2 % (lined 0.5 %). Away from buildings 5 % for 10 ft (6 in fall, IBC 1804.4), impervious 2 %. FFE >= 0.5-1 ft
  above adjacent grade and >= 1 ft above overflow/flood WSE.
- Typical maximums: mowed turf 3:1 (4:1 preferred), planted 2:1 (steeper needs geotech/stabilisation), parking 5 %,
  driveways 10-15 %; grade breaks over ~8-10 % need a vertical curve/transition.
- ADA 2010 / ICC A117.1: accessible route running slope <= 1:20 (5 %); steeper is a ramp: <= 1:12, rise <= 30 in
  (760 mm) per run, landings >= 60 in long, clear width >= 36 in, handrails if rise > 6 in. Cross slope <= 1:48
  (design ~1.5 % for tolerance). Curb ramp <= 1:12, flares <= 1:10, top landing 36 in. Accessible stalls and aisles
  <= 1:48 every direction; car 96 in + 60 in aisle, van 132 in + 60 in (or 96 + 96). Recompute slopes from spot
  elevations along the actual path; never trust a slope label.

## 2. Earthwork volumes (to SUBGRADE = finished grade minus pavement/topsoil section; stripping 4-12 in separate)
- Average end area V = L (A1 + A2)/2 per station interval; ft3/27 = yd3. Prismoidal V = L (A1 + 4Am + A2)/6
  (Am from mid-section dimensions, not the mean of A1 and A2); AEA overestimates pyramid-like shapes.
- Grid method, square cells area A, corner depths h: V = (A/4)(sum h1 + 2 sum h2 + 3 sum h3 + 4 sum h4), hn = corner
  shared by n cells; cut and fill separately, split cells on the 0-line; cross-check with a TIN surface volume.
- Shrink/swell: loose LCY = BCY (1 + swell); compacted CCY = BCY (1 - shrink). Typical swell earth 20-30 %, clay
  30-40 %, rock 50-65 %; shrink earth 10-20 %; rock compacts to ~1.2-1.4 x bank. Bank needed = CCY/(1 - shrink);
  truck loads use LCY. Net balance = cut(bank) - fill/(1 - shrink); label every quantity bank/loose/compacted.

## 3. Roadway and parking geometry (AASHTO Green Book)
- Horizontal curve: T = R tan(Delta/2), L = pi R Delta/180, LC = 2R sin(Delta/2), E = R(sec(Delta/2) - 1),
  M = R(1 - cos(Delta/2)); PC = PI - T, PT = PC + L (stationed along the arc). Arc degree D = 5729.58/R (ft).
  Min radius R = V^2/(15(e + f)) US (mph, ft), V^2/(127(e + f)) SI (km/h, m). Typical lanes 10-12 ft, crown 1.5-2 %.
- Vertical curve (g in %): y(x) = y_PVC + g1 x/100 + (g2 - g1) x^2/(200 L); A = |g2 - g1|, K = L/A, middle ordinate
  E = A L/800, high/low point x = g1 L/(g1 - g2) from PVC, PVC = PVI - L/2.
- SSD = 1.47 V t + 1.075 V^2/a (ft; t = 2.5 s, a = 11.2 ft/s2); SI 0.278 V t + 0.039 V^2/a (a = 3.4 m/s2). Design
  SSD / crest K / sag K: 30 mph 200 ft/19/37; 40 mph 305/44/64; 50 mph 425/84/96; 60 mph 570/151/136.
  Crest: S < L: L = A S^2/2158 (SI 658); S > L: L = 2S - 2158/A. Sag (headlight): S < L: L = A S^2/(400 + 3.5S)
  (SI 120 + 3.5S); S > L: L = 2S - (400 + 3.5S)/A. Min L ~ 3V ft. Stalls 9 x 18 ft, 24 ft aisle; fire lane >= 20 ft.
- AASHTO 93 flexible: log10 W18 = ZR S0 + 9.36 log10(SN + 1) - 0.20 + log10(dPSI/2.7)/(0.40 + 1094/(SN + 1)^5.19)
  + 2.32 log10 MR - 8.07 (MR psi). ZR: 85 % -1.037, 90 % -1.282, 95 % -1.645; S0 0.45 flexible (0.35 rigid);
  dPSI = 4.2 - pt (pt 2.0-2.5). SN = a1 D1 + a2 m2 D2 + a3 m3 D3 (in); typical a1 0.44 HMA, a2 0.14 crushed base,
  a3 0.11 subbase, m 1.0; MR ~ 1500 CBR psi (fine soils). Solve SN iteratively, size layers top-down so the SN above
  each layer protects it, then apply agency minimum thicknesses. ESAL factor ~ (axle/18 kip)^4. Rigid: k, Sc, Ec, J, Cd.

## 4. Water and fire flow
- 1 psi = 2.31 ft water. Service 40-80 psi (PRV > 80); >= 20 psi residual everywhere at max day + fire flow; fire
  flow/duration per fire code (IFC App. B: 1,000 gpm small 1-2 family, >= 1,500 gpm others, 2-4 h).
- Hydrant test (NFPA 291): Q_R = Q_F ((S - R_target)/(S - R_test))^0.54. Hazen-Williams: hf = 10.67 L Q^1.852/
  (C^1.852 D^4.87) SI (m, m3/s); p = 4.52 Q^1.85/(C^1.85 d^4.87) psi per ft US (gpm, in). C: PVC 150, lined DI 130-140.
  V <= 5 ft/s normal, <= 10 ft/s fire. Mains typically 8 in (6 in min to hydrants), looped, valves at tees.
- Hydrants (typical, IFC 507.5/App. C): within 400 ft of all exterior walls along fire access (600 ft sprinklered or
  R-3); street spacing 300-500 ft; FDC within 100 ft of a hydrant; 3-5 ft behind curb, clear of obstructions.

## 5. Sanitary sewer (Ten States Standards typical)
- Min slopes for 2 ft/s full (n = 0.013): 8 in 0.40 %, 10 in 0.28 %, 12 in 0.22 %, 15 in 0.15 %, 18 in 0.12 %,
  21 in 0.10 %, 24 in 0.08 %. Main >= 8 in; building sewer 4-6 in at 1/8-1/4 in/ft; max V ~10-15 ft/s. Flow = avg
  (e.g. 100 gpcd) x Harmon PF = 1 + 14/(4 + sqrt(P)) (P thousands) + I/I; peak depth <= 0.5-0.75 D.
- Manholes at every change of grade, size, direction, junction and line end; spacing <= 400 ft (<= 15 in), <= 500 ft
  (18-30 in). Drop across MH ~0.1 ft straight, ~0.2 ft at bends; match crowns on size increase; drop connection when
  inlet >= 24 in above outlet invert. Recompute slope = (inv up - inv down)/length for every reach.
- Separation: water-sewer >= 10 ft horizontal edge to edge; at crossings water >= 18 in above sewer, one full water
  pipe length centred on the crossing; otherwise pressure-rated sewer/encasement per state rules.

## 6. Erosion and sediment control / SWPPP
- EPA CGP (or state permit) at >= 1 ac disturbed or part of a common plan: NOI, SWPPP on site, inspection every
  7 days (or 14 days + within 24 h of >= 0.25 in rain), stabilisation begun when work stops >= 14 days and finished
  within 14 days (7 in sensitive waters); final = 70 % uniform perennial cover; then NOT.
- BMPs in sequence: stabilised entrance, perimeter silt fence/wattles (fence on contour, ~1/4 ac per 100 ft, J-hooks)
  and inlet protection BEFORE clearing; traps (< ~5 ac) and basins (>= 10 ac to one point: 3,600 ft3/ac drained or
  2-yr 24-h runoff); dewatering filtration, washout, stockpile cover, check dams, blankets on slopes >= 3:1; remove
  perimeter controls after stabilisation. Show phasing, details, maintenance and responsible party.

## 7. Hydrology beyond the rational method (NRCS TR-55/TR-20)
- S = 1000/CN - 10 in (SI 25400/CN - 254 mm); Ia = 0.2 S; Q = (P - 0.2S)^2/(P + 0.8S) if P > Ia else 0. Volume
  (ac-ft) = Q(in) A(ac)/12. Typical CN (HSG A/B/C/D): impervious 98; open space good 39/61/74/80; woods good
  30/55/70/77; 1/4-ac lots 61/75/83/87. Split pervious/impervious runoff when CNs differ widely. Rain: NOAA Atlas 14.
- Tc = sum of Tt: sheet flow (<= 100 ft) Tt = 0.007 (nL)^0.8/(P2^0.5 s^0.4) h (L ft, P2 = 2-yr 24-h in, s ft/ft;
  n smooth 0.011, short grass 0.15, dense grass 0.24, woods 0.4-0.8); shallow concentrated V = 16.13 s^0.5 unpaved,
  20.33 s^0.5 paved (ft/s); channel/pipe by Manning; Tt = L/(3600 V) h. Minimum Tc 0.1 h.
- SCS unit hydrograph: lag = 0.6 Tc, Tp = D/2 + lag (D ~ 0.133 Tc), qp = 484 A Q/Tp (cfs, mi2, in, h) [SI
  0.208 A Q/Tp: m3/s, km2, mm, h], base ~2.67 Tp; convolve incremental excess for the storm hydrograph.
- Detention (modified Puls): 2S2/dt + O2 = I1 + I2 + 2S1/dt - O1, dt <= Tp/5. Stage-storage by average-area/conic;
  orifice Q = Cd A sqrt(2 g h) (Cd ~0.6, h to centroid); rectangular weir 3.33 (L - 0.1nH) H^1.5, V-notch
  2.5 tan(theta/2) H^2.5 (US). Post <= pre (or agency rate) for every design storm; peak outflow must fall on the
  inflow recession limb; peak stage below the spillway crest. WQv = P Rv A/12 ac-ft, Rv = 0.05 + 0.009 I (I %
  impervious), P = 90th pct storm (often 1.0 in); drawdown 24-48 h (<= 72); channel protection 24-h ED of 1-yr storm.

## 8. Floodplain (FEMA NFIP) and final cross-checks
- Zones A (no BFE), AE (BFE), AO/AH shallow, VE coastal, X shaded 0.2 %/unshaded. P(>= 1 event in n yr) = 1 -
  (1 - 1/T)^n (100-yr in 30 yr = 26 %). Floodway: no rise (0.00 ft) by HEC-RAS + certification, else CLOMR/LOMR;
  fringe fill often needs 1:1 compensatory storage; lowest floor >= BFE + local freeboard (1-2 ft, ASCE 24); convert
  FIRM datum to plan datum before comparing.
- Before issue: same elevations, inverts, stations, sizes on plan/profile/details/calcs/quantities; cite each limit.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(

    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320

REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(

DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row

            buf = []
    if buf:

def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]

# DCBim IFC deliverable contract (v1.0)

Your deliverable is **`submission/model.ifc`** — an ISO-10303-21 (STEP
Physical File) text file, schema **IFC4**, expressing your site design as
a BIM model. It is machine-graded: the grader tessellates your solids
(ifcopenshell 0.8.5), projects them to the ground plane, and runs the
same site-layout verifier as the 2D benchmark on the result. Geometry is
NEVER read from attributes or psets — only from the solids. A complete
worked example demonstrating every rule below is `docs/example.ifc`.

## File-level gates (verdict IFC_INVALID)

| rule | failure code |
|---|---|
| parses as STEP / IFC4 (`FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'))`) | `file:parse_error`, `file:schema` |
| exactly one `IfcProject` | `file:project_count` |
| project length unit is SI **METRE** (`IFCSIUNIT(*,.LENGTHUNIT.,$,.METRE.)`) | `units:not_metre`, `units:no_length_unit` |
| scene extent within 5x of the parcel extent (catches mm/unit errors) | `scale:scale_implausible` |

## Model structure

- One `IfcSite` aggregated under the project (`IfcRelAggregates`);
  every building aggregated under the site.
- One `IfcBuilding` per required program building (e.g. DH1, SUB1 ...).
- Each building needs a Body `IfcShapeRepresentation`
  (`'Body','SweptSolid'`) containing an `IfcExtrudedAreaSolid`:
  footprint polygon as an `IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef` over an
  `IfcPolyline` (coordinates in metres, world/site coordinates —
  placements are honored, identity placement is simplest), extruded
  along +Z. The grader accepts any representation it can tessellate,
  but the projected footprint must be ONE simple polygon.

## Per-building gates (verdict EXTRACTION_FAILED)

| rule | failure code |
|---|---|
| tessellatable Body representation | `<name>:no_body` |
| solid volume > 0 | `<name>:zero_volume` |
| projected footprint is one simple polygon | `<name>:multi_polygon` |
| footprint has no holes | `<name>:holes` |
| at least one IfcBuilding in the file | `file:no_buildings` |

## Height convention (above-grade rule)

Extracted building height = **max Z of the solid**. Normal buildings:
extrude from z=0 up (top = your intended height). Ground works with
required height 0 (e.g. stormwater retention): extrude BELOW grade
(e.g. z in [-0.3, 0]) so max Z = 0.

## Identity pset (per building): `DCD_Layout`

Attach via `IfcRelDefinesByProperties` -> `IfcPropertySet` named
`DCD_Layout` with `IfcPropertySingleValue`s:
  - `LayoutId`   (IfcText)    e.g. "DH1"  — the id used by the graph
  - `LayoutType` (IfcText)    e.g. "data_hall" — a program type
  - `Phase`      (IfcInteger) phase number (1 if unphased)
The building's `Name` attribute should equal LayoutId (fallback source).

## Networks pset (on the IfcSite): `DCD_Networks`

Roads / MV routing / graph are NOT modeled as IFC entities in v1.0.
Serialize them as ONE property `json` (IfcText) on a pset named
`DCD_Networks` on the IfcSite: a JSON string of the form
`{"networks": [...], "graph": {...}}` following exactly the
`output_schema.networks` / `output_schema.graph` contract in
agent_view.json (same schema as the 2D benchmark; JSON quotes must be
escaped per STEP string rules — apostrophes doubled).

## v1.1 additions: storeys, GFA, semantic gate

- **Storeys are real entities.** Every building of a use with a required
  GROSS floor area (see the program and brief Addendum A) must contain one
  `IfcBuildingStorey` per storey, aggregated under the building
  (`IfcRelAggregates`), with `Elevation` values inside the solid's z-range
  (ground storey at 0). Storey count is read from these entities — never
  from attributes. GFA = measured footprint area x storey count.
- **`DCD_Layout` gains `GrossFloorAreaM2` (IfcReal)** for storeyed uses;
  it must match measured footprint x storeys within 1%.
- **Semantic gate (verdict SEMANTICS_INVALID):** missing storeys on a
  storeyed use, storey elevations outside the solid, duplicate elevations,
  missing pset keys, GrossFloorAreaM2 missing/mismatched, or any
  BoundingBox representation. The oracle reports only `semantics:failed`
  — diagnosing which rule you broke is part of the task.
- **Coarse gate codes:** file/extraction failures report the failing item
  only (e.g. `DH1:invalid`, `units:invalid`) — not the failure category.

## Grading after extraction

Identical to the 2D benchmark: schema -> geometry -> constraint bundle
-> objective (`1.0*mv_cable_length + 0.3*road_length`, computed from
your DCD_Networks polylines; building-derived checks from your solids).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent checker: re-read submission/model.ifc (IFC4 STEP) and test every hard requirement."""
import json, math, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp/ahpele/bin")
import ahpele_ifc as A

IFC = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/app/files/frontier__DCBim__p6_002/submission/model.ifc"
text = open(IFC, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
schema, ents = A.parse(text)
val = A.val

def attrs(eid):
    name, args = ents[eid]
    key = A.ALIASES.get(schema, schema)
    sch = A.SCHEMAS.get(key, {})
    spec = sch.get(name)
    if not spec:
        return {}
    names = [a.split(":")[0] for a in spec if a != "!abstract"]
    return dict(zip(names, args))

def one(t):
    return [i for i, (n, a) in ents.items() if n == t]

def refs(v):
    if isinstance(v, A.Ref): return [int(v)]
    if isinstance(v, list):
        out=[]
        for x in v: out += refs(x)
        return out
    if isinstance(v, A.Typed): return refs(v.args[0]) if v.args else []
    return []

def poly_area(poly):
    a=0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1,y1=poly[i]; x2,y2=poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]
        a += x1*y2-x2*y1
    return abs(a)/2

def centroid(poly):
    a=0.0; cx=0.0; cy=0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1,y1=poly[i]; x2,y2=poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]
        cr=x1*y2-x2*y1; a+=cr; cx+=(x1+x2)*cr; cy+=(y1+y2)*cr
    a*=0.5
    return (cx/(6*a), cy/(6*a))

def seg_point_d2(ax,ay,bx,by,px,py):
    dx=bx-ax; dy=by-ay; L2=dx*dx+dy*dy
    if L2==0: return (px-ax)**2+(py-ay)**2
    t=max(0.0,min(1.0,((px-ax)*dx+(py-ay)*dy)/L2))
    qx=ax+t*dx; qy=ay+t*dy
    return (px-qx)**2+(py-qy)**2

def point_in_poly(px,py,poly):
    inside=False; j=len(poly)-1
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        xi,yi=poly[i]; xj,yj=poly[j]
        if ((yi>py)!=(yj>py)) and (px < (xj-xi)*(py-yi)/(yj-yi)+xi):
            inside=not inside
        j=i
    return inside

def point_poly_dist(px,py,poly):
    if point_in_poly(px,py,poly): return 0.0
    return math.sqrt(min(seg_point_d2(poly[i][0],poly[i][1],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)][0],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)][1],px,py) for i in range(len(poly))))

def seg_seg_intersect(a,b,c,d):
    def o(p,q,r): return (q[0]-p[0])*(r[1]-p[1])-(q[1]-p[1])*(r[0]-p[0])
    o1,o2,o3,o4=o(a,b,c),o(a,b,d),o(c,d,a),o(c,d,b)
    return ((o1>0)!=(o2>0)) and ((o3>0)!=(o4>0)) and 0 not in (o1,o2,o3,o4)

def seg_poly_dist(a,b,poly):
    if point_in_poly(a[0],a[1],poly) or point_in_poly(b[0],b[1],poly): return 0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        if seg_seg_intersect(a,b,poly[i],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]): return 0.0
    return min(min(point_poly_dist(a[0],a[1],poly),point_poly_dist(b[0],b[1],poly)),
               min(seg_point_d2(a[0],a[1],b[0],b[1],p[0],p[1])**0.5 for p in poly))

def poly_poly_dist(p,q):
    if any(point_in_poly(x,y,q) for x,y in p) or any(point_in_poly(x,y,p) for x,y in q): return 0.0
    return min(min(seg_poly_dist(p[i],p[(i+1)%len(p)],q) for i in range(len(p))),
               min(seg_poly_dist(q[i],q[(i+1)%len(q)],p) for i in range(len(q))))

def seg_len(g):
    return sum(math.hypot(g[i+1][0]-g[i][0],g[i+1][1]-g[i][1]) for i in range(len(g)-1))

def path_len_pts(g): return seg_len(g)

# ---- extract buildings
B={}
for bid in one("IFCBUILDING"):
    a=attrs(bid); nm=str(val(a.get("Name")))
    pds=refs(a.get("Representation"))[0]
    pa=attrs(pds); sr=refs(pa.get("Representations"))[0]
    sa=attrs(sr); ext=None
    for it in refs(sa.get("Items")):
        if ents[it][0]=="IFCEXTRUDEDAREASOLID": ext=it
    ea=attrs(ext); prof=refs(ea.get("SweptArea"))[0]
    pf=attrs(prof); curve=refs(pf.get("OuterCurve"))[0]
    ca=attrs(curve)
    if ents[curve][0]=="IFCPOLYLINE":
        pts=[tuple(float(v) for v in attrs(p)["Coordinates"][:2]) for p in refs(ca.get("Points"))]
    else:
        raise SystemExit("unexpected profile curve "+ents[curve][0])
    if len(pts)>1 and pts[0]==pts[-1]: pts=pts[:-1]
    pos=attrs(refs(ea.get("Position"))[0]); loc=attrs(refs(pos.get("Location"))[0])
    zbase=float(loc["Coordinates"][2]); depth=float(val(ea.get("Depth")))
    B[nm]={"id":bid,"name":nm,"poly":pts,"area":poly_area(pts),"centroid":centroid(pts),
           "zbase":zbase,"depth":depth,"top":zbase+depth,"pset":{},"storeys":[]}

# psets / storeys
for rid in one("IFCRELDEFINESBYPROPERTIES"):
    a=attrs(rid); objects=refs(a.get("RelatedObjects")); ps=refs(a.get("RelatingPropertyDefinition"))[0]
    pa=attrs(ps); pname=str(val(pa.get("Name")))
    props={}
    for pr in refs(pa.get("HasProperties")):
        q=attrs(pr); props[str(val(q.get("Name")))]=val(q.get("NominalValue"))
    for o in objects:
        if ents[o][0]=="IFCBUILDING":
            nm=str(val(attrs(o).get("Name"))); B[nm]["pset"][pname]=props
        if ents[o][0]=="IFCSITE" and pname=="DCD_Networks":
            SITE_NET=props
for rid in one("IFCRELAGGREGATES"):
    a=attrs(rid); parent=refs(a.get("RelatingObject"))[0]; kids=refs(a.get("RelatedObjects"))
    if ents[parent][0]=="IFCBUILDING":
        nm=str(val(attrs(parent).get("Name")))
        for k in kids:
            if ents[k][0]=="IFCBUILDINGSTOREY":
                B[nm]["storeys"].append(float(val(attrs(k).get("Elevation"))))

# ---- networks
payload=json.loads(str(SITE_NET["json"]))
nets=payload["networks"]; graph=payload["graph"]

# ---- site data
AV=json.load(open("/app/files/frontier__DCBim__p6_002/agent_view.json"))
site=AV["site"]; parcel=site["parcel"]; ex=site["exclusions"]; receptors=site["receptors"]
fails=[]; warns=[]; util=[]
def check(ok,msg,detail=""):
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ")+msg+(("  ["+detail+"]") if detail else ""))
    if not ok: fails.append(msg+" "+detail)
def note(msg): print("     "+msg)

# IFC gates
check(len(one("IFCPROJECT"))==1,"IFC exactly one IfcProject")
check(schema=="IFC4","IFC schema %s"%schema)
units=[attrs(i) for i in one("IFCSIUNIT")]
check(any(str(val(u.get("UnitType")))=="LENGTHUNIT" and str(val(u.get("Name")))=="METRE" for u in units),"SI length unit METRE")
check(len(one("IFCSITE"))==1,"IFC one IfcSite")
check(len(B)==7,"seven program buildings: "+",".join(sorted(B)))
# scene extent
allx=[p[0] for b in B.values() for p in b["poly"]]; ally=[p[1] for b in B.values() for p in b["poly"]]
check(max(allx)-min(allx)<=5*320 and max(ally)-min(ally)<=5*280,"scene extent within 5x parcel")

# program & geometry
need={"DH_P1":("data_hall",1,4500,7200),"DH_P2":("data_hall",2,4500,7200),"SUB":("substation",1,1000,None),
      "GEN":("generator_yard",1,500,None),"CTP":("cooling_plant",1,800,None),"BRM":("berm",1,300,None),"RET":("stormwater_retention",1,100,None)}
for nm,(typ,ph,amin,gfa) in need.items():
    check(nm in B,"building %s exists"%nm)
    if nm not in B: continue
    b=B[nm]; p=b["pset"].get("DCD_Layout",{})
    check(str(p.get("LayoutType"))==typ,f"{nm} LayoutType {typ}",str(p.get("LayoutType")))
    check(int(float(p.get("Phase",-1)))==ph,f"{nm} Phase {ph}",str(p.get("Phase")))
    check(b["area"]>=amin-1e-6,f"{nm} area >= {amin}",f"{b['area']:.3f}")
    check(b["top"]<=13.8+1e-9,f"{nm} height <= 13.8",f"{b['top']:.3f}")
    check(b["depth"]>0,f"{nm} volume positive",f"depth {b['depth']}")
    check(abs(float(p.get("HeightM",-9))-b["top"])<1e-6,f"{nm} HeightM matches solid top",str(p.get("HeightM")))
    if gfa:
        check(len(b["storeys"])>=1,f"{nm} has storeys",str(b["storeys"]))
        check(all(b["zbase"]-1e-9<=e<=b["top"]+1e-9 for e in b["storeys"]),f"{nm} storey elevations inside solid",str(b["storeys"]))
        check(len(set(b["storeys"]))==len(b["storeys"]),f"{nm} unique storey elevations")
        eff=len(b["storeys"])
        check(eff>=2,f"{nm} GFA via storeys >= {gfa}",f"area*storeys={b['area']*eff:.1f}")
        check(abs(float(p.get("GrossFloorAreaM2",-9))-b["area"]*eff)<=0.01*b["area"]*eff,f"{nm} GFA pset matches footprint x storeys",f"{p.get('GrossFloorAreaM2')} vs {b['area']*eff:.2f}")
        if eff>1:
            ff=b["top"]/eff
            check(3.2-1e-9<=ff<=5.5+1e-9,f"{nm} floor-to-floor {ff:.3f} in 3.2-5.5")
        w=max(max(x for x,y in b["poly"])-min(x for x,y in b["poly"]),max(y for x,y in b["poly"])-min(y for x,y in b["poly"]))
        h=min(max(x for x,y in b["poly"])-min(x for x,y in b["poly"]),max(y for x,y in b["poly"])-min(y for x,y in b["poly"]))
        check(w/h<=2.5+1e-9,f"{nm} aspect <= 2.5",f"{w/h:.3f}")
        check(b["area"]>=4500,f"{nm} area >=4500",f"{b['area']:.1f}")

# setbacks (basins/berms exempt)
for nm,b in B.items():
    if nm in ("BRM","RET"): continue
    xs=[p[0] for p in b["poly"]]; ys=[p[1] for p in b["poly"]]
    d=min(min(xs),min(ys),320-max(xs),280-max(ys))
    check(d>=18-1e-9,f"{nm} 18 m lot-line setback",f"min {d:.3f}")

# footprint cap
foot=sum(b["area"] for nm,b in B.items() if nm not in ("BRM","RET"))
check(foot<=0.151*320*280+1e-6,"aggregate footprint <= 15.1%",f"{foot:.1f} / {0.151*320*280:.1f}")
note(f"footprint incl berm+ret = {sum(b['area'] for b in B.values()):.1f} (exempt components excluded)")

# wetland buffers (structure polygons, including berm/ret)
for nm,b in B.items():
    for w in ex:
        d=poly_poly_dist(b["poly"], [tuple(p) for p in w["polygon"]])
        check(d>=w["buffer_m"]-1e-9,f"{nm} outside {w['id']} buffer",f"{d:.2f} m")

# road network
roads=[n for n in nets if n["type"]=="road"]
check(len(roads)>=1,"road network present")
road=roads[0]; rw=max(float(n["width_m"]) for n in roads)
# combine all road polylines for continuous-network checks (they join within 2 m)
rg=[roads[0]["geom"][0]] + [p for n in roads for p in n["geom"][1:]]
check(all(len(n.get("geom",[]))>=2 for n in nets),"every network has >=2 points")
check(all(seg_len(n["geom"])>0 and min(math.hypot(n["geom"][i+1][0]-n["geom"][i][0],n["geom"][i+1][1]-n["geom"][i][1]) for i in range(len(n["geom"])-1))>=0.5-1e-9 for n in nets if len(n["geom"])>=2),"no network segment shorter than 0.5 m")
# entrance
check(min(math.hypot(p[0]-q[0],p[1]-q[1]) for p in rg for q in [(p[0],0.0)])<=2+1e-9,"road touches south frontage within 2 m")
check(all(0<=p[0]<=320 and 0<=p[1]<=280 for p in rg),"road inside parcel")
# road clears wetland buffers taking width into account
for w in ex:
    d=min(seg_poly_dist(rg[i],rg[i+1],[tuple(p) for p in w["polygon"]]) for i in range(len(rg)-1))
    check(d>=w["buffer_m"]+rw/2-1e-9,f"road centreline clear of {w['id']} buffer + half width",f"{d:.2f}")

# access Schedule C
for nm in B:
    b=B[nm]
    d=min(seg_poly_dist(b["poly"][i],b["poly"][(i+1)%len(b["poly"])],rg) if False else
          min(point_poly_dist(p[0],p[1],b["poly"]) for p in rg) for i in range(1))
    # distance polygon to road polyline (min over road segment to building polygon)
    d=min(seg_poly_dist(rg[i],rg[i+1],b["poly"]) for i in range(len(rg)-1))
    check(d<=18+1e-9,f"{nm} within 18 m of access road",f"{d:.2f}")

# generator separation
for nm in ("DH_P1","DH_P2","SUB","CTP"):
    d=poly_poly_dist(B["GEN"]["poly"],B[nm]["poly"])
    check(d>=28-1e-9,f"GEN >=28 m from {nm}",f"{d:.2f}")

# retention
core=sum(b["area"] for nm,b in B.items() if nm not in ("BRM","RET"))
road_area=sum(seg_len(n["geom"])*float(n.get("width_m",0)) for n in nets if n["type"]=="road")
req_core=0.118*(core+road_area)
req_all=0.118*(sum(b["area"] for b in B.values())+road_area)
note(f"impervious core={core:.1f} road={road_area:.1f}; required RET core-based={req_core:.1f}, all-buildings-based={req_all:.1f}; provided={B['RET']['area']:.1f}")
check(B["RET"]["area"]>=req_core-1e-9,"RET >=11.8% of core roofs + roads",f"{B['RET']['area']:.1f} >= {req_core:.1f}")
check(B["RET"]["area"]>=req_all-1e-9,"RET >=11.8% even if berm+RET counted",f"{B['RET']['area']:.1f} >= {req_all:.1f}")

# MV metrics
mvs=[n for n in nets if n["type"]=="mv_power"]
mv_len=sum(seg_len(n["geom"]) for n in mvs)
mv_p1=sum(seg_len(n["geom"]) for n in mvs if int(n.get("phase",0))==1)
mv_p2=sum(seg_len(n["geom"]) for n in mvs if int(n.get("phase",0))==2)
road_len=sum(seg_len(n["geom"]) for n in roads); road_p1=sum(seg_len(n["geom"]) for n in roads if int(n.get("phase",0))==1)
total=mv_len+0.3*road_len; p1=mv_p1+0.3*road_p1
note(f"MV total={mv_len:.3f} (P1 {mv_p1:.3f}, P2 {mv_p2:.3f}); road={road_len:.3f}; objective={total:.3f}; phase1={p1:.3f}")
check(total<=473+1e-9,"total MVP+0.3 road <=473",f"{total:.3f}")
check(p1<=314+1e-9,"Phase 1 MVP+0.3 road <=314",f"{p1:.3f}")
# MV no short segments / phase tags
check(all("phase" in n for n in nets),"every network phase-tagged")
check(all(int(n.get("phase",0)) in (1,2) for n in nets),"network phases 1/2")
# greatest straight-line distance served

straights=[math.dist(poc,sub)]+[math.dist(sub,B[x]["centroid"]) for x in ("DH_P1","DH_P2")]
check(mv_len>=max(straights)-1e-6,"MV length >= greatest straight-line distance",f"{mv_len:.2f} >= {max(straights):.2f}")
check(mv_len>=sum(straights)-1e-6,"MV length >= sum of straight-line legs (conservative reading)",f"{mv_len:.2f} >= {sum(straights):.2f}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate submission/model.ifc for DCBim p6_002 (IFC4 STEP, no BIM library)."""
import json, math, os

OUT = "/app/files/frontier__DCBim__p6_002/submission/model.ifc"

def area(poly):
    a = 0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1, y1 = poly[i]; x2, y2 = poly[(i + 1) % len(poly)]
        a += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
    return abs(a) / 2.0

def gid(n):
    return f"{n:022d}"

# Program buildings. Rectangles are CCW in world metres.
B = [
    dict(id="DH_P1", typ="data_hall", phase=1, h=9.0, storeys=2,
         poly=[(90.0, 18.5), (182.0, 18.5), (182.0, 67.4347826087), (90.0, 67.4347826087)]),
    dict(id="DH_P2", typ="data_hall", phase=2, h=9.0, storeys=2,
         poly=[(98.0, 190.0), (171.0, 190.0), (171.0, 251.6712328767), (98.0, 251.6712328767)]),
    dict(id="SUB", typ="substation", phase=1, h=6.0, storeys=1,
         poly=[(165.5, 82.0), (183.5, 82.0), (183.5, 137.84), (165.5, 137.84)]),
    dict(id="GEN", typ="generator_yard", phase=1, h=3.0, storeys=1,
         poly=[(203.0, 170.0), (233.0, 170.0), (233.0, 186.7), (203.0, 186.7)]),
    dict(id="CTP", typ="cooling_plant", phase=1, h=4.0, storeys=1,
         poly=[(203.0, 220.0), (243.0, 220.0), (243.0, 240.05), (203.0, 240.05)]),
    dict(id="BRM", typ="berm", phase=1, h=8.0, storeys=1,
         poly=[(173.0, 158.0), (178.0, 158.0), (178.0, 222.0), (173.0, 222.0)]),
    dict(id="RET", typ="stormwater_retention", phase=1, h=0.0, storeys=1,
         poly=[(204.5, 18.5), (279.5, 18.5), (279.5, 43.1666666667), (204.5, 43.1666666667)]),
]
for b in B:
    b["area"] = area(b["poly"])
    b["gfa"] = b["area"] * b["storeys"]

# Networks. All coordinates world metres.
networks = [
    {"id": "ROAD_P1", "type": "road", "width_m": 6.0, "phase": 1,
     "geom": [[187.0, 0.0], [187.0, 250.0]]},
    {"id": "MV_P1_UTIL", "type": "mv_power", "width_m": 0.0, "phase": 1,
     "geom": [[320.0, 195.0], [183.0, 110.0]]},
    {"id": "MV_P1_DH1", "type": "mv_power", "width_m": 0.0, "phase": 1,
     "geom": [[183.0, 110.0], [174.0, 72.0]]},
    {"id": "MV_P2_DH2", "type": "mv_power", "width_m": 0.0, "phase": 2,
     "geom": [[184.0, 110.0], [188.0, 150.0], [188.0, 250.0], [197.0, 250.0],
              [188.0, 241.0], [175.5, 230.0]]},
]
graph = {
    "nodes": ["DH_P1", "DH_P2", "SUB", "GEN", "CTP", "BRM", "RET", "GATE", "POC"],
    "edges": [
        {"u": "POC", "v": "SUB", "type": "utility_feed", "via": "MV_P1_UTIL"},
        {"u": "SUB", "v": "DH_P1", "type": "power_feed", "via": "MV_P1_DH1"},
        {"u": "SUB", "v": "DH_P2", "type": "power_feed", "via": "MV_P2_DH2"},
        {"u": "GATE", "v": "DH_P1", "type": "vehicle_access", "via": "ROAD_P1"},
    ],
}
payload = json.dumps({"networks": networks, "graph": graph}, separators=(",", ":"))
assert "'" not in payload

lines = []
def add(s): lines.append(s)
n = 1
add("ISO-10303-21;")
add("HEADER;")
add("FILE_DESCRIPTION(('ViewDefinition[DesignTransferView]'),'2;1');")
add("FILE_NAME('/dev/null','2026-07-26T23:00:16+00:00',(''),(''),'IfcOpenShell 0.8.5','IfcOpenShell 0.8.5','Nobody');")
add("FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'));")
add("ENDSEC;")
add("DATA;")

# fixed header entities
project = n; n += 1
unit_len = n; n += 1
unit_area = n; n += 1
unit_vol = n; n += 1
unit_assign = n; n += 1
pt0 = n; n += 1
dir_z = n; n += 1
dir_x = n; n += 1
axis0 = n; n += 1
context = n; n += 1
subcontext = n; n += 1
site = n; n += 1
rel_proj_site = n; n += 1

add(f"#{project}=IFCPROJECT('{gid(project)}',$,'dcbim_p6_002',$,$,$,$,(#{context}),#{unit_assign});")
add(f"#{unit_len}=IFCSIUNIT(*,.LENGTHUNIT.,$,.METRE.);")
add(f"#{unit_area}=IFCSIUNIT(*,.AREAUNIT.,$,.SQUARE_METRE.);")
add(f"#{unit_vol}=IFCSIUNIT(*,.VOLUMEUNIT.,$,.CUBIC_METRE.);")
add(f"#{unit_assign}=IFCUNITASSIGNMENT((#{unit_area},#{unit_vol},#{unit_len}));")
add(f"#{pt0}=IFCCARTESIANPOINT((0.,0.,0.));")
add(f"#{dir_z}=IFCDIRECTION((0.,0.,1.));")
add(f"#{dir_x}=IFCDIRECTION((1.,0.,0.));")
add(f"#{axis0}=IFCAXIS2PLACEMENT3D(#{pt0},#{dir_z},#{dir_x});")
add(f"#{context}=IFCGEOMETRICREPRESENTATIONCONTEXT($,'Model',3,1.0000000000000001E-05,#{axis0},$);")
add(f"#{subcontext}=IFCGEOMETRICREPRESENTATIONSUBCONTEXT('Body','Model',*,*,*,*,#{context},$,.MODEL_VIEW.,$);")
add(f"#{site}=IFCSITE('{gid(site)}',$,'SITE_p6_002',$,$,$,$,$,$,$,$,$,$,$);")
add(f"#{rel_proj_site}=IFCRELAGGREGATES('{gid(rel_proj_site)}',$,$,$,#{project},(#{site}));")

# Buildings and geometry
for b in B:
    bldg = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{bldg}=IFCBUILDING('{gid(bldg)}',$,'{b['id']}',$,$,$,#{bldg+13},$,$,$,$,$);")
    # 2D cartesian points + polyline profile
    pts = []
    for (x, y) in b["poly"] + [b["poly"][0]]:
        pid = n; n += 1
        pts.append(pid)
        add(f"#{pid}=IFCCARTESIANPOINT(({x:.6f},{y:.6f}));")
    polyline = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{polyline}=IFCPOLYLINE(({','.join('#%d' % p for p in pts)}));")
    profile = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{profile}=IFCARBITRARYCLOSEDPROFILEDEF(.AREA.,$,#{polyline});")
    if b["id"] == "RET":
        zbase, depth = -0.3, 0.3
    else:
        zbase, depth = 0.0, b["h"]
    spt = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{spt}=IFCCARTESIANPOINT((0.,0.,{zbase:.6f}));")
    axis = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{axis}=IFCAXIS2PLACEMENT3D(#{spt},#{dir_z},#{dir_x});")
    edir = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{edir}=IFCDIRECTION((0.,0.,1.));")
    solid = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{solid}=IFCEXTRUDEDAREASOLID(#{profile},#{axis},#{edir},{depth:.6f});")
    shape = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{shape}=IFCSHAPEREPRESENTATION(#{subcontext},'Body','SweptSolid',(#{solid}));")
    pds = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{pds}=IFCPRODUCTDEFINITIONSHAPE($,$,(#{shape}));")
    # storeys, one relation per storey
    for st_i in range(b["storeys"]):
        st = n; n += 1
        sr = n; n += 1
        elev = 0.0 if st_i == 0 else 4.5 * st_i
        add(f"#{st}=IFCBUILDINGSTOREY('{gid(st)}',$,'{b['id']}_S{st_i+1}',$,$,$,$,$,$,{elev:.6f});")
        add(f"#{sr}=IFCRELAGGREGATES('{gid(sr)}',$,$,$,#{bldg},(#{st}));")
    # property set
    props = []
    for pname, pval in (("LayoutId", f"IFCLABEL('{b['id']}')"),
                        ("LayoutType", f"IFCLABEL('{b['typ']}')"),
                        ("Phase", f"IFCINTEGER({b['phase']})"),
                        ("HeightM", f"IFCREAL({b['h']:.6f})"),
                        ("GrossFloorAreaM2", f"IFCREAL({b['gfa']:.6f})")):
        pp = n; n += 1
        props.append(pp)
        add(f"#{pp}=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('{pname}',$,{pval},$);")
    pset = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{pset}=IFCPROPERTYSET('{gid(pset)}',$,'DCD_Layout',$,({','.join('#%d' % p for p in props)}));")
    relpset = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{relpset}=IFCRELDEFINESBYPROPERTIES('{gid(relpset)}',$,$,$,(#{bldg}),#{pset});")
    b["bldg_id"] = bldg

# site aggregates buildings
rel_site_bldgs = n; n += 1
add(f"#{rel_site_bldgs}=IFCRELAGGREGATES('{gid(rel_site_bldgs)}',$,$,$,#{site},({','.join('#%d' % b['bldg_id'] for b in B)}));")

# DCD_Networks pset on site
net_prop = n; n += 1
net_pset = n; n += 1
net_rel = n; n += 1

1. Project description
Design the schematic site layout for a two-hall data center campus on the parcel below (meters, local CRS). Two delineated wetlands flank a narrow upland corridor near the center of the site; the survey shows the corridor as the only practical route between the southern and northern developable areas. Program: two data halls (min 4,500 m2 each, aspect no greater than 2.5), one substation (min 1,000 m2), one diesel generator yard (min 500 m2), one cooling plant (min 800 m2), one landscape berm (min 300 m2), and stormwater retention. Utility power enters on the east lot line north of the eastern wetland. Residential receptors adjoin the site to the west (R1) and south (R2). Access is permitted only from the south street frontage. The campus is delivered in two phases: one data hall in Phase 1, the second (in the northern area) in Phase 2. Tag every building and utility line with its phase; each phase must independently comply.

2. Zoning and development standards
2.1 Retail and food-service uses shall provide one loading berth of at least 3.5 m by 12 m for each 2,500 m2 of gross floor area.
2.2 No building or structure shall exceed 45 m in height, measured from finished grade to the highest point of the roof structure.
2.3 Every building shall be set back not less than 18 m from each and every lot line. Stormwater management basins and landscape berms are exempt from yard requirements.
2.4 For parcels containing a designated heritage tree as recorded on the survey, a tree protection zone of 12 m radius shall be maintained free of construction.
2.5 The aggregate footprint of all buildings, exclusive of stormwater basins and berms, shall not exceed 15.1 percent of the gross lot area.

3. Fire and life safety
3.1 Apparatus access shall comply with Schedule C. Access roads shall form a continuous drivable network originating at the approved site entrance; isolated road segments shall not be credited toward compliance.
3.2 Hazardous-use yards shall be separated from occupied structures in accordance with Schedule B. For the purposes of this section, diesel generator yards and fuel storage areas are classified Class H-1, and every data hall, substation, cooling plant, office, and warehouse (including structures to remain) is an occupied structure.
3.3 Vehicular access shall be taken solely from the designated street frontage identified on the survey; no other curb cut will be permitted.

4. Environmental protection and stormwater
4.1 No structure shall be erected within 8 m of the delineated wetland (WET2), and no roadway shall cross it.
4.2 On-site stormwater retention shall provide surface area of not less than 11.8 percent of the total impervious area created, where impervious area comprises building roofs and paved roadways.
4.3 Where a mapped watercourse crosses the parcel, a riparian setback of 30 m from top-of-bank shall apply to all structures.
4.4 No structure shall be erected within 8 m of the delineated wetland (WET1), and no roadway shall cross it.
4.5 For sites within a designated FEMA Zone A floodplain, the lowest finished floor shall be elevated at least 0.6 m above base flood elevation.

5. Noise and visual standards
5.1 The cumulative sound level attributable to on-site mechanical equipment, received at any identified residential receptor, shall not exceed 42.35 dB(A). Attenuation by intervening buildings or berms may be credited.
5.2 Generator yards and fuel storage areas shall not be directly visible from any identified receptor location; screening may be provided by intervening buildings or berms. Stormwater basins shall not be credited as screening.

6. Utilities and design-to-cost
6.1 Where a public sanitary sewer is available within 60 m of the parcel, connection thereto is required; the survey records no such main within 60 m.
6.2 The total drawn length of the connected medium-voltage system shall be no less than the greatest straight-line distance it serves (from the point of interconnection to the substation, and from the substation to each data hall).
6.3 Separate medium-voltage lines shall be deemed a single connected system where they join one another within the stated join tolerance, or where each terminates at the substation, which functions as a common bus.
6.4 Design-to-cost: the weighted utility quantity, computed as the routed medium-voltage length in metres plus three tenths of the roadway length in metres, shall not exceed 473.
6.5 A medium-voltage distribution system shall be routed continuously from the utility point of interconnection through the substation to every data hall, shown both as drawn lines and as typed edges of the connectivity graph. Routed lengths shall be physically plausible for the distances served; token or disconnected line segments shall not be credited.

7. Phasing and existing structures
7.1 Phase 1 utility quantities are separately capped: the weighted sum of Phase 1 medium-voltage length (x1.0) and Phase 1 roadway length (x0.3) shall not exceed 314.
7.2 Model home complexes in residential subdivisions may be occupied prior to final plat recordation subject to a surety bond.
7.3 Where development is phased, every building and utility line shall be tagged with its phase, and the Phase 1 scope, taken alone, shall fully comply with every requirement of this document. Compliance of Phase 1 shall not depend on Phase 2 construction.
7.4 Phase 1 shall comprise only the Phase 1 scope: building types allocated to Phase 2 by the program shall not be constructed in Phase 1 beyond the count allocated to Phase 1.
7.5 Facilities constructed in an earlier phase shall remain in service, unaltered, at full build-out; accordingly, no utility line shall be routed beneath the footprint of a building of a different phase.

8. Drawing and submission standards
8.1 Network segments shall be treated as joined where they lie within 2 m of one another; no drawn segment may be shorter than 0.5 m.
8.2 All survey monuments disturbed by construction shall be reset by a licensed land surveyor within 30 days.
8.3 Utility connections shall be drawn to within 5 m of the structures they serve.
8.4 The site entrance shall be drawn to within 2 m of the designated frontage line.

Schedule B - Hazard separation distances
  Class H-1 (standby generation; fuel storage): 28 m to any occupied structure
  Class H-2 (bulk flammable liquids over 40 m3): 45 m to any occupied structure
  Class H-3 (compressed-gas storage over 2,000 kg): 30 m to any lot line

Schedule C - Apparatus access
  Occupied and hazardous-use structures: within 18 m of a conforming access road
  Open-lot storage under 100 m2: within 60 m
  Unoccupied utility cabinets: exempt

Submission: return JSON per the output schema (buildings with polygon footprints and phase tags where applicable; networks as polylines with widths and phase tags; typed connectivity graph). All requirements of this document are mandatory; requirements that do not apply to the recorded site conditions or the stated program impose no obligation.

ADDENDUM A — 3D MASSING AND BIM CONDITIONS
A.1 Required GROSS FLOOR AREAS (all storeys): DH_P1: 7 200 m2; DH_P2: 7 200 m2. Footprint minimums remain in force.
A.2 Generator yards and fuel storage shall be screened from direct view from the marked viewpoints; screening is effective only where the intervening structure or berm is tall enough to intercept the line of sight (viewer eye height 1.7 m).
A.3 Each building shall provide the gross floor area required by the program for its use (GFA = footprint area x storey count).
A.4 No structure shall exceed 13.8 m in height above grade; berms and at-grade basins are exempt.
A.5 For multi-storey uses, floor-to-floor height (building height divided by storey count) shall be between 3.2 m and 5.5 m.
A.6 Data-hall rooftop mechanical plant is a noise source (sound power per program schedule) located at roof level; barrier credit applies only where an intervening structure is tall enough to break the line of sight from the roof to the receptor."

Design the data-center site specified in **`agent_view.json`** — read it
first. It contains the site geometry (`site`), the building program
(`program`), objective weights (`objective`), the `output_schema` for the
networks/graph payload, and `brief_document`: the DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS
AND CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL. Coordinates are meters in a local CRS. The
design problem (constraints, objective) is identical to the 2D site-layout
benchmark; what changes is the deliverable:

Your deliverable is **`submission/model.ifc`** — an IFC4 BIM model (STEP
text) of the site: one IfcBuilding with an extruded-solid footprint per
program building, identity psets, and the roads/MV/graph payload embedded
as the `DCD_Networks` pset on the IfcSite. The FULL contract is
**`docs/ifc_contract.md`**; **`docs/example.ifc`** is a complete worked
example (toy site) demonstrating every convention — study it. A stub
model.ifc (valid header, site, no buildings) is provided.

There are NO BIM libraries in this workspace. Producing valid IFC STEP
text is part of the task.

**Every numeric limit that binds your design lives ONLY in the prose of
`brief_document`** — setbacks, separations, noise limits, sizing rules,
access requirements. Some clauses reference schedules elsewhere in the
document; follow the chain. Some clauses do not bind this particular
site; deciding which is part of the task.

## Verification protocol (metered L1 oracle)

The verifier is NOT in this workspace. Your ONLY feedback channel is:

```
python3 oracle_client.py submission/model.ifc
```

- **Budget: 20 calls for this task.** Each call uploads your model. IFC
  gate failures return the verdict (`IFC_INVALID` /
  `EXTRACTION_FAILED`) plus `item:code` tokens (see the contract table).
  Once your model extracts, calls return the design verdict
  (`FEASIBLE | INFEASIBLE | SCHEMA_INVALID | GEOMETRY_INVALID`), the
  failing layer, and failing constraint ids (composites expand, e.g.
  `c12[c1,c8]`). No margins, no distances.
- Call 21 and later are refused (HTTP 429). There is no other oracle
  access and no local verifier.
- **Your session is graded on the BEST design among all oracle-checked
  models plus your final `submission/model.ifc`** (ordered by layer
  reached, then constraint fraction, then lower objective). Every model
  you send counts; a late bad edit cannot erase an earlier good design.

Budget strategy is part of the task: reason the design AND the IFC
serialization to correctness on paper before spending calls, then repair
surgically from the failure codes.

A task pass requires verdict `FEASIBLE` on your final design (every
binding condition satisfied; IFC gates, schema and geometry are hard
gates). Partial credit is one half of the constraint fraction of your
final extracted design. The weighted objective
(`1.0 * mv_cable_length + 0.3 * road_length`) does not change the
score: feasibility is what is graded.

"""Generate submission/model.ifc for DCBim p6_002 (IFC4 STEP, no BIM library)."""
import json, math, os

OUT = "/app/files/frontier__DCBim__p6_002/submission/model.ifc"

def area(poly):
    a = 0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1, y1 = poly[i]; x2, y2 = poly[(i + 1) % len(poly)]
        a += x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
    return abs(a) / 2.0

def gid(n):
    return f"{n:022d}"

# Program buildings. Rectangles are CCW in world metres.
B = [
    dict(id="DH_P1", typ="data_hall", phase=1, h=9.0, storeys=2,
         poly=[(90.0, 18.5), (182.0, 18.5), (182.0, 67.4347826087), (90.0, 67.4347826087)]),

    dict(id="SUB", typ="substation", phase=1, h=6.0, storeys=1,

    dict(id="GEN", typ="generator_yard", phase=1, h=3.0, storeys=1,

]
for b in B:

# Networks. All coordinates world metres.
networks = [
    {"id": "ROAD_P1", "type": "road", "width_m": 6.0, "phase": 1,

    {"id": "MV_P1_DH1", "type": "mv_power", "width_m": 0.0, "phase": 1,
     "geom": [[183.0, 110.0], [174.0, 72.0]]},
    {"id": "MV_P2_DH2", "type": "mv_power", "width_m": 0.0, "phase": 2,

]
graph = {
    "nodes": ["DH_P1", "DH_P2", "SUB", "GEN", "CTP", "BRM", "RET", "GATE", "POC"],
    "edges": [
        {"u": "POC", "v": "SUB", "type": "utility_feed", "via": "MV_P1_UTIL"},
        {"u": "SUB", "v": "DH_P1", "type": "power_feed", "via": "MV_P1_DH1"},

assert "'" not in payload

add("FILE_NAME('/dev/null','2026-07-26T23:00:16+00:00',(''),(''),'IfcOpenShell 0.8.5','IfcOpenShell 0.8.5','Nobody');")
add("FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'));")

add("DATA;")

project = n; n += 1
unit_len = n; n += 1
unit_area = n; n += 1
unit_vol = n; n += 1
unit_assign = n; n += 1
pt0 = n; n += 1
dir_z = n; n += 1
dir_x = n; n += 1

add(f"#{axis0}=IFCAXIS2PLACEMENT3D(#{pt0},#{dir_z},#{dir_x});")

    polyline = n; n += 1
    add(f"#{polyline}=IFCPOLYLINE(({','.join('#%d' % p for p in pts)}));")

    spt = n; n += 1

    key = A.ALIASES.get(schema, schema)
    sch = A.SCHEMAS.get(key, {})
    spec = sch.get(name)
    if not spec:
        return {}
    names = [a.split(":")[0] for a in spec if a != "!abstract"]
    return dict(zip(names, args))

def one(t):
    return [i for i, (n, a) in ents.items() if n == t]

def refs(v):
    if isinstance(v, A.Ref): return [int(v)]
    if isinstance(v, list):
        out=[]
        for x in v: out += refs(x)
        return out
    if isinstance(v, A.Typed): return refs(v.args[0]) if v.args else []
    return []

def poly_area(poly):
    a=0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1,y1=poly[i]; x2,y2=poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]
        a += x1*y2-x2*y1
    return abs(a)/2

def centroid(poly):
    a=0.0; cx=0.0; cy=0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        x1,y1=poly[i]; x2,y2=poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]
        cr=x1*y2-x2*y1; a+=cr; cx+=(x1+x2)*cr; cy+=(y1+y2)*cr
    a*=0.5
    return (cx/(6*a), cy/(6*a))

def seg_point_d2(ax,ay,bx,by,px,py):
    dx=bx-ax; dy=by-ay; L2=dx*dx+dy*dy
    if L2==0: return (px-ax)**2+(py-ay)**2
    t=max(0.0,min(1.0,((px-ax)*dx+(py-ay)*dy)/L2))
    qx=ax+t*dx; qy=ay+t*dy
    return (px-qx)**2+(py-qy)**2

def point_in_poly(px,py,poly):
    inside=False; j=len(poly)-1
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        xi,yi=poly[i]; xj,yj=poly[j]
        if ((yi>py)!=(yj>py)) and (px < (xj-xi)*(py-yi)/(yj-yi)+xi):
            inside=not inside
        j=i
    return inside

def point_poly_dist(px,py,poly):
    if point_in_poly(px,py,poly): return 0.0
    return math.sqrt(min(seg_point_d2(poly[i][0],poly[i][1],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)][0],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)][1],px,py) for i in range(len(poly))))

def seg_seg_intersect(a,b,c,d):
    def o(p,q,r): return (q[0]-p[0])*(r[1]-p[1])-(q[1]-p[1])*(r[0]-p[0])
    o1,o2,o3,o4=o(a,b,c),o(a,b,d),o(c,d,a),o(c,d,b)
    return ((o1>0)!=(o2>0)) and ((o3>0)!=(o4>0)) and 0 not in (o1,o2,o3,o4)

def seg_poly_dist(a,b,poly):
    if point_in_poly(a[0],a[1],poly) or point_in_poly(b[0],b[1],poly): return 0.0
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        if seg_seg_intersect(a,b,poly[i],poly[(i+1)%len(poly)]): return 0.0
    return min(min(point_poly_dist(a[0],a[1],poly),point_poly_dist(b[0],b[1],poly)),
               min(seg_point_d2(a[0],a[1],b[0],b[1],p[0],p[1])**0.5 for p in poly))

def poly_poly_dist(p,q):
    if any(point_in_poly(x,y,q) for x,y in p) or any(point_in_poly(x,y,p) for x,y in q): return 0.0
    return min(min(seg_poly_dist(p[i],p[(i+1)%len(p)],q) for i in range(len(p))),
               min(seg_poly_dist(q[i],q[(i+1)%len(q)],p) for i in range(len(q))))

def seg_len(g):
    return sum(math.hypot(g[i+1][0]-g[i][0],g[i+1][1]-g[i][1]) for i in range(len(g)-1))

def path_len_pts(g): return seg_len(g)

    B[nm]={"id":bid,"name":nm,"poly":pts,"area":poly_area(pts),"centroid":centroid(pts),

need={"DH_P1":("data_hall",1,4500,7200),"DH_P2":("data_hall",2,4500,7200),"SUB":("substation",1,1000,None),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}
    if v == int(v):
        out.add(str(int(v)))
    return out


def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]
